correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the product and nilpotent radical: J^2=Ann(J)=W. The rank-one Rota–Baxter equation reduces to f(x)f(y)a^2=(f(x)f(ay)+f(y)f(ax))a. In odd characteristic a central generator imposes no condition; a noncentral generator requires a^2=0 and f(aJ)=0. Smoothness makes aJ=W for every noncentral square-zero generator. Counting image lines and compatible nonzero functionals gives (q+1)(q^6-1)+q^2(q^4-1)#C(k) without overlap. The complete-intersection and explicit Weierstrass embedding are smooth including infinity; elliptic Frobenius theory yields zeta recovery. Brute force over F_3 verified all 529984 pairs of nonzero a,f against the original basis-pair identity and counted 5792 maps; independent field tests and F_9 arithmetic corroborate. Finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The prior central-extension construction and general rank-one tensor identity are not new. The checked closest results classify nilpotent Jordan algebras up to dimension four, order-two/three semigroup-algebra Rota–Baxter operators, or complex spectral-parameter operators from elliptic vector bundles. They do not imply the exact rank-one census on six-dimensional square-zero central extensions with arbitrary smooth pencils, its universal realization of elliptic curves, or trace/zeta recovery. Targeted indexed and published-claim searches found no decisive dominating statement; this is a provisional priority judgment rather than proof from search absence.

value.rationale: The natural rank-one weight-zero Rota–Baxter census of a six-dimensional nilpotent algebra is determined across all smooth quadratic pencils; its noncentral contribution equals a nonconstant elliptic point-count invariant. Every odd-characteristic elliptic curve occurs via the explicit degree-four model, so the operator count recovers the Frobenius trace, zeta function and counts over all extensions. Over F_5 examples have the same algebra dimension and nilpotency class but distinct operator counts 124944, 156144 and 218544, demonstrating arithmetic information not fixed by simple algebra dimensions. This is a motivated uniform invariant and recovery phenomenon, not a routine small enumerative check.
